title: add-constrained-retrieval-quickstart-and-cli-runner
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a developer-facing quickstart for constrained retrieval RAG workflows with an offline-first CLI runner, sample data, and telemetry hooks for Redwood Console. Non-breaking; docs and examples only.
description: Context: teams building retrieval-augmented generation frequently need patterns for constrained retrieval (budgeted token windows, timebound indexes, and candidate pruning) to meet latency and cost targets. This quickstart provides a compact, opinionated template demonstrating windowed retrieval, candidate scoring, and a tiny offline CLI runner so engineers can iterate locally without provisioning cloud infra. Motivation: reduce developer onboarding time for production-practices that combine retrieval constraints, lightweight vector stores, and streaming generation. What this PR includes: 1) a new quickstart directory with README, step-by-step tutorial, and a minimal dataset; 2) an opinionated CLI tool (rust/ts shim) that runs indexing, constrained retrieval, and a simulated Redwood API streaming client; 3) examples showing SQLite+annlite and an in-memory L2 fallback; 4) telemetry hooks that emit compact probe events to the Redwood Console local adaptor; 5) a small eval harness and smoke tests used by CI. Checklist: [x] README tutorial and architecture diagram embedded as ASCII; [x] CLI with commands: index, query, replay; [x] sample prompt sets and stepwise assertions for constrained retrieval; [x] telemetry probes and a lightweight local console sink; [x] unit + integration CI jobs; [x] docs site cross-link from quickstarts index. Compatibility notes: quickstart targets the hosted SDK surface (TS/Python snippets included) and runs entirely offline for demo purposes. It also shows how to swap to a hosted Redwood index by changing one ENV variable. Security: sample dataset contains synthetic content only. Limitations: not intended as production vector DB guidance; guidance section points to Dedicated/Private docs for scale. High-level usage: git clone; cd quickstarts/constrained-retrieval; yarn install || python -m venv; ./rcli index sample-data.json; ./rcli query --prompt "Summarize constraints" --budget-tokens 512. This single-string description includes motivation, scope, and brief usage to remain concise in the PR page.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial scaffold and README; add sample dataset and indexer; implement CLI commands index/query/replay; add telemetry adaptor and sample sink; add TS/Python snippet examples; add CI smoke tests; polish docs and cross-links.
